title: The Last Night of 33
description:
On the last night of the first year, the notebook, phone, and folded receipts each occupied a strip of the desk in the room where {name} now lived. Beneath its first line — "{notebook_motive}" — ran "3 billion won. Five years" and twelve months of figures: rent, transit, money in, losses. People's names were wedged between numbers. Days when he had failed to meet them appeared nowhere.

{name} moved between the phone's total assets, {assets}, and the first page. The goal written on the first day of the year had not been erased, but that figure could no longer explain the year by itself.

Four minutes to midnight. The last minutes before the date changed passed across the phone screen. {name} divided the final page and wrote two headings: "Kept" and "Postponed." Whichever side he filled first, the other would remain empty tonight.

description_if_known.kept_clean_hands:
On the last night of the first year, {name} set the first notebook page beside the phone. Beneath "{notebook_motive}" and "3 billion won. Five years" came twelve months of rent, transit, money in, and losses.

The two million won from the first month was absent. After blocking the offer to lend out his account, {name} had set a 4:20 a.m. alarm. Money never taken left no figure, and the ledger alone did not show how he had spent the hours afterward.

Total assets: {assets}. The conversation list held the names of people he had met this year beside messages he had never answered. Four minutes to midnight, {name} divided the last page into "Kept" and "Postponed." Calling his hands clean did not fill either column for him.
description_if_known.escaped_dirty_money:
On the last night of the first year, {name} reread "{notebook_motive}" and "3 billion won. Five years." The two million won taken in the first month and the later receipt for a 1.5 million won return sat on separate lines.

After learning that victims' money had passed through his account, he blocked the numbers and closed it. Even after the 1.5 million won return was accepted, requests for further confirmation and the scope of his responsibility remained. No single figure said what was over and what was not.

Total assets: {assets}. Beside that number were promises kept and messages unanswered. Four minutes to midnight, {name} divided the last page into "Kept" and "Postponed." Filling either side first would not erase the figures on the other.
description_if_known.fell_to_darkness:
On the last night of the first year, {name} moved down the page beneath "{notebook_motive}" and "3 billion won. Five years." Two million won in the first month; three million after that. Only the amounts occupied the income column. The sources were blank.

The recruiter contacted him from a new number and sent the next account number. The three sets {name} had handed over already occupied amount fields; the new message remained at the top of the conversation list.

Total assets: {assets}. Unanswered names remained in the conversation list. Four minutes to midnight, {name} divided the last page into "Kept" and "Postponed." The pen would not descend under either heading.
description_if_known.jaehyuk_scammed:
December.

The year Jaehyuk disappeared. The year the account ran dry. The year of the real bottom.

The first line of the notebook still read, "{notebook_motive}" Most of the numbers beneath it had been erased.

Still here, though.

Looked at the ceiling of the room where he lived now. Its outline remained after the light went out.
description_if_known.entered_network:
December.

The year of meeting Im Sangchul's people. Learning a little of how that world works.

Under the notebook's first line, "{notebook_motive}," names he had never known a year ago had multiplied.

What that means going forward — still unknown.

Looked at the ceiling of the room where he lived now. Its outline remained after the light went out.
description_if_known.hit_rock_bottom:
December.

The year of seeing the real bottom. Now {name} knows exactly where it is.

Eraser dust clung to the notebook's first line, "{notebook_motive}" He had not erased the sentence.

Climbed back from it. Not all the way — but back.

Looked at the ceiling of the room where he lived now. Its outline remained after the light went out.

description_memory_if_known.m3_ledger_reasons_named: Following the brief reasons on the March page brought the days and hours behind twelve months of figures back into view.
description_memory_if_known.m3_ledger_totals_only: The March total was exact. Everything it could not count still had to be written separately.
description_memory_if_known.obligation_receipt:demo_collision:select: On Friday of Week 24, {name} called his father first. He still learned neither the diagnosis nor when he might go to Changwon, but he wrote down when to call again.

On Friday of Week 24, {name} sent the first month-end discrepancy sheet assigned to him at Hanbit Distribution at 5:59 p.m. He left unverified figures for a Monday site recheck instead of inventing them.

On Friday of Week 24, {name} submitted the City Facilities worksheet. In Week 28, a text with the same application number said there would be no interview. The submission and its result now stood on the same line.
On Friday of Week 24, {name} submitted the City Facilities worksheet and received an automated confirmation. The work itself was now part of his application record.
On Friday of Week 24, {name} reached the store in time for Daeun's night shift. Their check-in stopped whenever a customer entered, but {name} was the one who had gone to see her.
On Friday of Week 24, {name} messaged Jaehyuk first and asked about his week. Their conversation, with no talk of money, continued past six.
On Friday of Week 24, {name} left Sangchul's business card in the drawer and reconciled his own spending first. Rent, food, transit, and phone payments remained together on one ledger page.
On Friday of Week 24, {name} took an urgent overnight loading shift and earned 280,000 won. The day's pay and the strain in his palms and lower back entered the same ledger.
On Friday of Week 24, {name} set one alarm and put the phone face down. With every problem still unresolved, he chose sleep instead of pushing through one more night.
description_memory_if_known.obligation_receipt:demo_collision:deferr: That day, he neither called his father nor set a time for the next call.
The first month-end discrepancy sheet assigned to him at Hanbit Distribution passed its six o'clock deadline. One duty from that first assigned close remained as a blank in the notebook.
The City Facilities worksheet was not submitted. There was no automated receipt, and no result to wait for.
Though he knew when Daeun worked nights, {name} did not go to the store that day. The check-in he could have offered first was left for later.
{name} could have checked in with Jaehyuk first, but he did not start the conversation that day. Unsent words left no trace in the Kakao chat list.
The month's receipts stayed on the desk, and {name} did not reconcile his spending. Finding out where his own money had gone was postponed too.
{name} did not take the urgent overnight loading shift. Neither the 280,000 won nor the strain it would have left in his palms and lower back appeared in the ledger.
Lying down and tending to his body was pushed aside. The year's final page held not only the work he finished, but another night he endured.

choices.text: Finish the notebook — postpone sleep and record every gain beside what it cost
choices.result_text:
{name} spread the receipts by date and wrote the name postponed beside each amount. One line read "Gained," the next "Given up." Neither total resolved cleanly.

Past midnight, he erased neither the first promise nor the three billion won. By the time he glued down the last receipt, the celebration outside had stopped. One corner of the paper slowly lifted.

choices.text: Call Father for New Year's — close the ledger without settling it tonight
choices.result_text:
{name} closed the notebook and tapped Father's contact. Father answered on the second ring. "Did you eat?" "Not yet." "Eat before the year's over." Neither of them mentioned three billion won or the old debt.

It was past midnight when the call ended. A receipt slid from the cover behind the desk. {name} did not turn on the light to find it.

choices.text: Turn off both notebook and phone — answer nothing and sleep tonight
choices.result_text:
{name} reopened neither the conversation list nor tomorrow's date before switching off the phone. The notebook closed with both "Kept" and "Postponed" empty.

A countdown came through the wall after the light went out. He kept his eyes closed from ten to one. Even after the year changed, his hand did not emerge from beneath the blanket.

title: The Last Night of 34
description:
On the last night of the second December, {name} cleared the desk and opened his notebook. The phone displayed total assets of {assets}. The calendar and conversations retained twelve months of replies actually sent and appointments made, erased, or missed. Some lines began with names. Others ended in amounts. Some were blank.

{name} divided a new page into three spaces: "One appointment to keep next year," "What money and people cost," and "Distance left to the target." Whatever he had acquired and whoever he had met, the only things guaranteed on the desk tonight were the notebook, the phone, and an unwritten first line.

The pen moved between the three spaces. Closing the second year did not mean knowing every answer. It meant choosing what his own hand would carry into the first space of the new year.

description_if_known.year1_resolve:
On the last night of the second December, {name} reread the sentence on the final page of the previous year: keep what was gained and what was surrendered on the same page. This year's record held completed dates beside postponed ones. The total assets of {assets} on the phone counted only what had become money.

{name} did not clean up the page. He did not push lines beginning with names beneath the figures or fill blank spaces with some other success. He divided a new page into three parts and lifted the pen. Again, the task was not to manufacture an elegant answer. It was to stop pretending a line had never existed simply because it did not fit.
description_if_known.year1_numb:
On the last night of the second December, {name} turned past the final page left blank a year ago and opened this year's record. Total assets of {assets}. Times when replies were sent. Appointments eventually erased. There were records, but no sentence that held them together.

Deleting every notification would leave a clean screen. Closing the notebook would hide every blank. But feeling nothing was different from closing something in order not to feel. {name} wrote only three headings — "Appointments," "Costs," and "Target" — then stopped. The first line he chose would be the year's final answer.
description_if_known.jaehyuk_stood_up:
On the last night of the second December, {name} passed Jaehyuk's name in the phone and opened the year's total assets of {assets}. The figures had continued after he stood up again. He had not, however, returned to the self who trusted before the fall. No profit-and-loss screen held that fact.

In the notebook he wrote three headings: "What to trust again," "What to repay first," and "Who to keep next year." None proved the others. {name} left the spaces blank and raised the pen. The first line of the new year needed to name what he would take responsibility for, not declare that he had recovered well.
description_if_known.chose_money_over_father:
On the last night of the second December, {name} found the time stamp from the day he had chosen money first. Something real had been kept by that choice; at the same hour, a name had gone unanswered. Total assets of {assets} counted only the first.

Calling it wrong in one line would turn what he had actually protected into a lie. Calling it right would erase the unanswered time again. {name} divided the notebook into three spaces: next year's schedule, the cost to money and people, and the target. Whichever one he wrote first, the other two remained.
description_if_known.crossed_line:
On the last night of the second December, {name} checked the amount from the day he crossed a line. The number was exact. The line itself appeared on no screen. Income and spending, promises and cancellations had continued as usual afterward. Nothing stopping had made the choice look smaller than it was.

Total assets: {assets}. {name} started to write, "The time I will stop next time," then lifted the pen. Knowing a line and actually stopping at it were different acts. The first space of the new year required one action to keep, not another vow.

choices.text: Carry one appointment he will keep into the first space of the new year
choices.result_text:
From the year's record, {name} chose one person he could still contact. He wrote a date and time in the first open week, then added beneath the name: Confirm first, then arrive.

One calendar space closed. The asset total did not move, but the first line of the new page held a time he had to keep before it held an amount.

choices.text: Put the cost to money and the cost to people on the same page
choices.result_text:
On the left, {name} copied the money that had actually entered and left. On the right, he copied the time spent replying, visiting, and waiting. He wrote only what the record could prove and drew a short line through what he could not remember.

The two sides did not become one total. {name} folded the page corner to mark an unfinished reckoning. Even after the notebook closed, that corner protruded slightly beyond the cover.

choices.text: Close the other spaces and write only the distance left to the target
choices.result_text:
{name} ruled through the "Appointments" and "Costs" spaces, then copied the target screen into the notebook: current assets, amount remaining, months left. Without names, three lines were enough.

The arithmetic became clean when the notebook closed. Even after the display went dark, the last figure lingered in the black glass. {name} turned the phone facedown and did not reopen the notebook.

title: One Line to Carry into the New Year
description:
Twenty-three minutes before midnight, {name} spread out only the records the second year had left. Each door entered through another person—or deliberately left closed—carried one real name, address, or time. The Changwon hospital record held only what happened: an opened time, a deferred date, or a cost sent instead.

Four lines sat on top: a bill, an arrangement with Father, the source of an earlier door, and a person to keep next year. Only one or two had completion times. The rest showed deferral, expiration, or an untouched blank.

{name} opened the new year's first page. He could not carry all four first. One real remainder—not a claim about what he had done well—had to take the opening space.

choices.text: Carry the current status of the bill and payment record into the first space of the new year
choices.result_text:
{name} copied the line with its real amount, due date, and payment status unchanged to the top of the new page. He neither reduced the figure nor erased whose choice had created it. In the first action space he wrote: Compare the original with the current status, and settle any amount that remains.

The other records stayed behind the folded page. What appeared first in the new year was not the target amount, but the current state of a bill that had already arrived.

choices.text: Carry over the person or source in the door or remaining-address record
choices.result_text:
From the door or remaining-address record, {name} copied one unerased line exactly: a person's name, an address, or the source that had put it before him. Beneath it he wrote questions instead of a verdict: Why did this reach me? What price went unnamed?

{name} neither called nor went anywhere yet. He left one calendar space open so the first check of the new year would verify that name, address, or source instead of another number.

choices.text: Carry over first the promise to the person he will keep
choices.result_text:
{name} circled one line that still held a person's name and found the earliest time he could clear in the new calendar. Beside the name, he wrote both the time and whether he would call or go in person.

The unfinished spaces remained. One open hour in the first week of the year went back to that person first, and {name} traced the border twice so no other appointment could enter it.

choices.text: Ask everyone still waiting for one extension
choices.result_text:
{name} opened each conversation named by a line that had not yet closed. In words suited to each person, he admitted he had missed the original date and asked for one new deadline.

He did not erase the postponement marks or claim an expired line had returned to life. Only the sent time was added beside each entry. What he finished before midnight was not the extension itself, but the act of no longer hiding that he was late.

title: The Last Night of 35
description:
On the last night of 35, a low, cold wind skimmed the Han River. At the railing, {name} woke the phone: total assets, the gap to the goal, one hundred weeks left. The figures stood in immaculate rows.

Two documents reopened that year remained in the Downloads folder: the application bearing Jaehyuk's name and Father's old guarantee. One held {name}'s signature; the other, Father's faded one. The shape was the same — the name of someone who trusted another person pushed into the box for the person who would carry the liability.

Below them were conversations that had never quite ended: an old friend, Father, and the last sentence from the person who heard what {name} had done with the truth this year. Knowing the facts was supposed to simplify a relationship. Instead, good and bad, victim and perpetrator, opportunity and trap refused to separate inside the same face.

Choosing had been easier before knowing. Now every option showed what it would discard first, the way the black water remained visible beneath Gangnam's light.

For the two years left, {name} had to decide whether the target and both documents would remain on the same screen, or whether the papers would be locked away so only the number remained. Each gust made the two signatures tremble in turn.

description_if_known.father_confession_heard:
The last night of 35. Between gusts over the river, Dad's voice seemed to return, even the slow breath before the secret finally came out.

Dad had spoken Im Sangchul's name. It had taken nearly a decade to say it. Long after the call ended, {name} kept holding the blank screen.

As a child, {name} thought one careless signature had destroyed the family. Now the person before that signature, and the words that nudged Dad toward it, were known. It was the same man now opening doors for {name}.

Even after the truth, Sangchul's advice remained precise and his opportunities retained value. Anger was supposed to make the relationship simple. Instead, every meeting demanded another choice.

{name} remembered the calls made to Dad and the coffee consumed across from Sangchul. One man's silence and another man's kindness occupied opposite sides of the same debt.

Dad's name sat below the target amount on the phone. Three billion won was still necessary. Now two questions had to be asked separately: who was it for, and whose methods would create it?

The Han River was dark. There was no return to ignorance. The next two years would be spent trying to beat Sangchul without learning to win like him.
description_if_known.sangchul_truth_known:
The last night of 35. Wind slipped through {name}'s coat. The hand on the railing tightened.

This year, Im Sangchul's name appeared beside the record of Dad's ruin. Two worlds that had seemed separate had shared one line for years.

Even after that discovery, Sangchul's advice remained precise, and the doors he opened still had value. Truth did not end the relationship. It forced a new choice every time.

Jaehyuk's face overlapped his. A victim first, then someone who drew in new victims. Sangchul spoke as though that transformation were ordinary.

{name} remembered how often people had been sorted into opportunities and costs this year. The vow not to resemble Sangchul and the habits already resembling him occupied the same body.

The lights across the river held steady, but their reflections kept breaking apart. A single beam became dozens when it touched the water.

Sangchul could still be beaten in the two years ahead. The harder task was not learning from him how to win.
description_if_known.arc_y3_jiyeon_departure_seen:
The last night of 35. When train lights passed across the far bank, the photo of Jiyeon's one-way ticket to Busan returned.

She had left Seoul to live under her own name. Not abandoning what she had, but stepping beyond its shadow.

{name} did not reread the message sent that day. Whether it released her or tried to hold her, the train had departed at the same time. Only the unsent words remained in Seoul.

Jiyeon had shown that courage could mean changing a goal. Finishing the first road chosen was not the only form of resolve.

{name} looked at the remaining distance to Gangnam, then turned off the screen. Was this goal truly chosen, or had years of pursuit merely made it feel personal?

Light on the river broke and joined again with every wave. A broken line had not vanished. It had changed direction.

Spending the next two years on the same road and spending them as the same person were different questions.
description_if_known.year2_confident:
The last night of 35. A year ago, {name} had believed the run was finally on track. The numbers had begun to resemble the plan.

This year tested that confidence: a trusted friend's pitch, a mentor's paper, the vertigo after typing the goal amount. Each pulled at the speed.

On track had been a comforting phrase. It sounded as though motion alone guaranteed arrival. In reality, every decision came with a lever that could change the rails.

The choices worth undoing remained clearer than the choices worth praising. Confidence survived, but it was no longer innocent.

The exact shortfall glowed on the phone. Everything paid to create that number refused to total neatly on any calculator.

The lights across the river resembled last year's. The eyes watching them had changed. They no longer believed that walking toward light sent every shadow harmlessly behind.

Still on track. Now {name} had begun to look at where the rails passed, too.
description_if_known.year2_conflicted:
The last night of 35. A year ago, {name} thought something had been gained and something lost. The reckoning was postponed because it felt too complicated.

Another year had not simplified it. Instead, it revealed what had been excluded from the math: someone's waiting, the silence after a call, the nights spent avoiding a mirror.

{name} moved between the asset total and the conversation list. Both recorded the year. One reduced it to rises and falls; the other preserved it as unread sentences.

Once, these could be kept in separate ledgers. Money choices in one, human choices in another. This year proved they occupied the same page.

That knowledge slowed the hand. Before what a choice would gain, {name} now saw the person it would make next.

Light fractured across the Han River. The things ignored for being complicated were still there, even in pieces.

There was no answer yet. But not knowing and pretending not to know were no longer the same thing.

choices.text: Keep both documents in one folder — carry the uncomfortable facts beside the goal
choices.result_text:
{name} moved the application and guarantee into one folder. He named it only with the date, adding neither lesson nor promise. The target amount remained too.

Side by side, the files showed different modification times. Nearly a decade lay in one row between Father's guarantee and this year's application. {name} left the screen on and looked across the river.

choices.text: Print both documents and seal them together — preserve the weight without forcing a verdict
choices.result_text:
At a nearby convenience store, {name} printed both files. Without rereading them, he put the sheets into one envelope. He neither threw it away nor wrote a conclusion tonight.

Inside the coat, one thin corner pressed against his ribs. When he released the railing, the cold had left a mark on his palm and the envelope a rectangle against his chest.

choices.text: Lock the documents and leave only the target screen — look at money next year
choices.result_text:
{name} moved both files into a locked folder and cleared every conversation alert. Only the remaining distance to the target occupied the first screen. While his hands moved, there was nothing to judge.

The phone stayed quiet as he turned his back on the river. The water kept sounding behind him, but {name} did not enter the password again.

title: The Last Night of 36
description:
On the last night of 36, {name} took the stairs to the roof. His notebook held both the times of what he had actually completed and the blanks left by what he had missed. Two weeks earlier, he had already acted on what he would protect in the final year.

Tonight did not ask him to choose again among a person, his body, and family. What lay open on the railing was not a set of options but the ledger after that choice. Only verifiable facts—a canceled schedule, a confirmation notice, a bill answered—could cross into the final year's first line.

Each gust lifted the blanks first. {name} had only to decide how he would carry four years of records into the next chapter.

description_if_known.arc_y4_year_close_protected_relationship:
On the last night of 36, {name} opened the notebook on the rooftop railing. Two weeks earlier, he had secured actual time for a person and canceled the overlapping money work. The calendar kept both the date he would honor and the speed he had surrendered.

He would not choose that boundary again tonight. He would carry the price into the final year's first line without secretly restoring the canceled work or using a person's name as an excuse.

Each gust lifted the time he had left open first.
description_if_known.arc_y4_year_close_protected_body:
On the last night of 36, {name} opened the notebook on the rooftop railing. The follow-up time he had confirmed for his own body two weeks earlier was printed on the notice inside his coat. The money work delayed by it remained on the calendar.

He would not choose again whether to protect his body. He would carry the slower pace into the final year's first line without canceling the confirmation or pretending the warning had never been real.

Each gust pressed the edge bearing the appointment time against his finger.
description_if_known.arc_y4_year_close_protected_family:
On the last night of 36, {name} opened the notebook on the rooftop railing. One line held the issuer, amount, deadline, and response limit of the family bill he had verified two weeks earlier. The shortfall he had refused to cover with someone else's name remained as it was.

He would not choose again whether to protect family. He would carry both the range he answered and the range he could not answer onto the final year's first page.

Each gust lifted the bill's folded corner first.
description_if_known.arc_y4_midpoint_receipt_seen:
On the last night of 36, {name} opened the notebook on the rooftop railing. The three lines locked at midyear retained only what could be verified: one promise protected and two closed channels, his actual response to his body, and whether he reached the family table. He invented no fact for the damaged year-end record.

Tonight did not ask him to choose again among a person, his body, and family. He had only to decide how to carry the costs he could verify into the next chapter.

Each gust lifted the unknown spaces as unknown spaces.
description_if_known.year3_weighted:
On the last night of 36, {name} began counting the floors halfway up to the roof. The envelope holding last year's two documents remained inside the notebook. This year's clinic notice and the name of the last person contacted lay on top.

The ability to feel a burden as a burden remained. He had begun to tell what could be put down as weight alone from what would make him lighter by taking part of him too. In the final year's calendar, work for the target, time for his body, and a date promised to someone demanded the same square.

{name} spread the blank calendar over the railing. Without one hand holding it down, the paper lifted. The cold left the same mark in his palm as last year.
description_if_known.year3_eyes_open:
On the last night of 36, {name} took the stairs to the roof. The two documents kept together at the Han River last year still remained unlocked. This year a clinic notice about his body and the name of the last person contacted had joined them.

Refusing to pretend had slowed every choice. But carrying everything visible also required space. With one year left, work for money, an examination postponed, and a date promised to someone occupied the same square.

{name} drew twelve months on the railing. Seeing Gangnam's light and the darkness beneath it together was no longer enough. Actual time now had to be assigned to one or the other.
description_if_known.year3_avoidant:
On the last night of 36, {name} paused for breath on the stairs to the roof. Since locking the files and clearing every conversation alert at the Han River, the screen had stayed quiet and his pace had increased. This year's clinic notice and the name of the last person contacted now appeared over that lock screen.

He remembered the relief after deleting the words before he remembered whose they were. The final year's calendar stayed neat if it held only work for money. Adding the examination and other people's time made the squares overlap.

{name} spread the blank calendar on the railing. Empty squares alone could not show whether he had been running forward or running away.
description_if_known.sangchul_truth_known:
The last night of 36.

Knew the truth, made the choices, watched the results accumulate.

Four years of decisions are what {name} is now.

Whether that's right or wrong — the ending hasn't come yet.
description_if_known.crossed_line:
The last night of 36.

There was a year a line got crossed. Something shifted gradually after that.

What's done is done. Took a long time to accept that.

Accepted now. This is just who {name} is.

choices.text: Enter even the blanks from four years—do not pretend the price disappeared
choices.result_text:
{name} wrote what he had kept and what he had missed in letters of the same size. He did not restore a schedule already canceled or invent a completion time for something left undone.

On the final line, he wrote: The cost is part of my record. Even when the wind lifted the paper, the ink hid neither side.

choices.text: Write the limits of what the final year can bear in money and time
choices.result_text:
{name} listed how much more money he could lose, which time could no longer move, and how many nights he could still surrender. He left the boundary protected two weeks earlier in place and marked only the new promises he could not accept beyond it.

The plan grew smaller and matched the facts. Gray rooftop concrete showed through one small blank.

choices.text: Write no verdict; seal the ledger and reopen it on the next chapter's first day
choices.result_text:
Without erasing a record, {name} placed the notebook and notices in one envelope. He wrote neither that he had been right nor that he would do everything next time.

On the envelope, he wrote only the date of the next chapter's first day. The wind stopped when the rooftop door closed.

title: Scene of the Year
description:
Before closing the first year's calendar, {name} turned through its scenes once more.

Not the best act or the worst one. Just the scene that would return first whenever this year was opened again.

Which one would remain?

choices.text: Choose a scene to keep
choices.result_text: One scene remained from the first year.

title: Scene of the Year
description:
The second year opened many doors. Some he entered. Some he turned away from.

{name} chose one scene instead of one result: the moment that would return before the numbers whenever he remembered this year.

choices.text: Choose a scene to keep
choices.result_text: One scene remained from the second year.

title: Scene of the Year
description:
What he learned could not become unknown again.

So {name} kept one scene instead of an explanation: the moment when this year's truth was clearest.

choices.text: Choose a scene to keep
choices.result_text: One scene remained from the third year.

title: Scene of the Year
description:
Time folded quickly that year. Some weeks vanished; a few seconds still carried weight.

{name} chose one scene that still held it.

choices.text: Choose a scene to keep
choices.result_text: One scene remained from the fourth year.

title: Scene of the Final Year
description:
The end of the calendar was visible. The ending had not arrived, but the final year already had a shape.

{name} chose the scene that would last longest — not to remember the ending, but the person who had reached it.

choices.text: Choose a scene to keep
choices.result_text: One scene remained from the final year.

title: No Longer in the Next Room
description:
At 11:51 p.m. on December 31, an 8:43 call with Hyunsu topped the screen. "The hallway sounds louder now that your room is empty, hyung." They avoided the exam and the new room, then hung up before midnight.

Receipts and notes from the year lay mixed on the desk. Some matched their dates, some held only names, and others remained blank. The notebook alone could not show what was missing. Its first line read "{notebook_motive}." Total assets were {assets}. On the last page, {name} wrote "People Contacted," "Work Finished," "Work Postponed," and "Left Blank." Only Hyunsu's call time and the records already written down could be verified now. Outside, a car passed with one long sound.

choices.text: Send Hyunsu the one line left unsaid on the call
choices.result_text:
{name} wrote, "I didn't say it before, but I remember the day I went to your door." Sent: 11:54 p.m.

Hyunsu replied, "That's heavy for a New Year's message, hyung," followed by a laughing mark. {name} copied it beside the call and left the other three headings blank.

choices.text: Move only the records that remain into date order and finish the first-year ledger
choices.result_text:
{name} moved only what remained on the screen and in the notebook into date order. Beside the 8:43 call with Hyunsu, he copied only numbers and names he could verify, drawing a short dash through every uncertain space.

No record stood in for another blank. Midnight arrived with the final line. Beyond the wall, someone clapped twice, late.

choices.text: Close the phone and notebook without deciding anything tonight
choices.result_text:
{name} switched off the screen with Hyunsu's call log still open and closed the notebook. Beneath its four headings remained one call time and only the records already written there.

The last page curled upward by degrees. Even after the countdown, the unwritten spaces stayed as they were.

title: One Square Left Open

description_memory_if_known.father_crisis_contact_present: The ticket, cancellation time, and chair beside the bed remained in the ledger. The visit was a relationship receipt for having moved in the crisis, not merit that decided the medical outcome.
description_memory_if_known.father_crisis_contact_called: The seconds of the connected ward call remained beside the distance he had not traveled to Changwon. The call did not decide the medical outcome, but it changed what he had actually done during the crisis.
description_memory_if_known.father_crisis_contact_missed: The ward's message and the time he replied that today was impossible remained side by side. He did not need to invent the unknown outcome for the time of his deferral to remain.

description:
The cafe had played its year-end closing announcement twice, but Daeun still sat across from {name} in her coat. The table held the actual times of what he had completed, the blanks left by what he had missed, a physical follow-up notice, and a family bill still waiting for an answer.

"Minjun, don't decide it with a promise this time. Do one thing now. Let me see what you cancel to make it real too."

Instead of explaining what he would protect in the final year, {name} had to complete one action with the phone and calendar.

choices.text: Cancel the overlapping night meeting and confirm Saturday evening with Daeun
choices.result_text:
{name} sent the cancellation to the night meeting first. Only after the delivery mark appeared did he save Saturday evening and show Daeun the calendar.

Before smiling, Daeun checked the cancellation time. "If a day comes when you can't make it, tell me before I have to wait."

Instead of a promise to protect the relationship, one money schedule actually closed.

choices.text: Book the physical follow-up in his own name and cancel the night work around it
choices.result_text:
{name} used the number on the notice to book the earliest follow-up in his own name. After the confirmation arrived, he removed the night work on both sides of it.

Daeun said, "Don't make it an appointment you need me to verify, Minjun. It's your body."

Without handing his care to Daeun, he left the time lost to the goal visible on the calendar.

choices.text: Verify the family bill's issuer, amount, and deadline, then answer with his own limit
choices.result_text:
{name} called the issuer and asked them to read the amount and deadline back to him. Beneath the verified text, he wrote the limit he could bear now and sent the answer. Daeun's name appeared nowhere.

Daeun looked at the arrival and response times side by side. "Now you can't end it by saying only that you paid."

The family bill became a responsibility with dates, not hidden debt.

title: A Correction Line from Busan

description_memory_if_known.father_crisis_contact_present: The ticket, cancellation time, and chair beside the bed remained in the ledger. The visit was a relationship receipt for having moved in the crisis, not merit that decided the medical outcome.
description_memory_if_known.father_crisis_contact_called: The seconds of the connected ward call remained beside the distance he had not traveled to Changwon. The call did not decide the medical outcome, but it changed what he had actually done during the crisis.

description:
Jiyeon in Busan and {name} at the desk in his current Seoul room opened the same calendar over a video call. What he had completed, what he had missed, a physical follow-up notice, and a family bill still waiting for an answer carried different timestamps.

"I can't verify 'I'll do my best.' oppa, do one thing now. Put what it delays on the same screen."

Jiyeon was not in Seoul. Without pretending the distance between Busan and Seoul had vanished, {name} had to complete one real action through the screen.

choices.text: Confirm the date in Busan and cancel the overlapping Seoul schedule now
choices.result_text:
{name} booked a seat to Busan for the date they had agreed on, then canceled the overlapping Seoul schedule. He placed the booking number and cancellation time on the same screen.

Jiyeon zoomed in. "Don't use my name as collateral for time. If you can't come, correct the record before passing the loss to me."

The long-distance promise remained in timestamps from two different cities, not in a claim that distance did not matter.

choices.text: Book the physical follow-up in his own name and show the delayed work beside it
choices.result_text:
{name} booked the follow-up in his own name and moved the delayed money work into the next cell. He placed the confirmation and lower projection on the same screen.

Jiyeon checked the figures once. "Don't calculate your body as an asset with no cost. The delay belongs in the plan if you want it to be accurate."

Even without Jiyeon taking over the care from Busan, the booking in Seoul was complete.

choices.text: Verify the family bill and deadline, then answer the issuer with his own limit
choices.result_text:
{name} called the issuer, verified the text, amount, and deadline, and sent the limit he could bear. He did not fill the shortfall with Jiyeon's name or their relationship.

Jiyeon pointed to the two timestamps. "When you learned and when you answered are terms too. That part is accurate now."

Only facts that could be checked across Busan and Seoul remained.

title: A Boundary Locked Alone

description_memory_if_known.father_crisis_contact_present: The ticket, cancellation time, and chair beside the bed remained in the ledger. The visit was a relationship receipt for having moved in the crisis, not merit that decided the medical outcome.
description_memory_if_known.father_crisis_contact_called: The seconds of the connected ward call remained beside the distance he had not traveled to Changwon. The call did not decide the medical outcome, but it changed what he had actually done during the crisis.

description:
Late at night, {name} opened the year's records at the desk in his current room. What he had actually completed, what he had missed, a physical follow-up notice, and a family bill still waiting for an answer carried different timestamps. The chair across from him was empty. No one's dialogue filled it.

No person absent from the current record arrived by default. Instead of a promise waiting for someone's approval, only actions {name} could complete alone remained.

He had to put one boundary for the final year into the actual calendar and call log, along with the work that would close because of it.

choices.text: Leave one hour next week for another person, then cancel the overlapping night work
choices.result_text:
{name} left one hour open in the following week's calendar and canceled the overlapping night work. He did not write who would receive the time. He did not fill the blank with a lover or friend the current record could not prove.

There was no one attached to the promise yet. Even so, one square left open for another person and the speed surrendered for it now existed.

choices.text: Book the physical follow-up in his own name and cancel the night work around it
choices.result_text:
{name} used the number on the notice to book the earliest follow-up in his own name. When the confirmation arrived, he removed the night work around it and saved the lower projection as it was.

There was no one to supervise or receive proof. Responsibility for his body and the slower figures both stayed with {name}.

choices.text: Verify the family bill's issuer, amount, and deadline, then answer with the limit he can bear
choices.result_text:
{name} called the issuer and verified the text, amount, and deadline. He neither promised to repay everything nor cover it with someone else's name. He sent the limit he could bear now.

When the call ended, both the response time and the range he could not answer remained. There was no heroic sentence that solved it, but the present boundary became fact.

title: The Last Night of 33
description:
On the last night of the first year, the notebook, phone, and folded receipts each occupied a strip of the desk in the room where {name} now lived. Beneath its first line — "{notebook_motive}" — ran "3 billion won. Five years" and twelve months of figures: rent, transit, money in, losses. People's names were wedged between numbers. Days when he had failed to meet them appeared nowhere.

{name} moved between the phone's total assets, {assets}, and the first page. The goal written on the first day of the year had not been erased, but that figure could no longer explain the year by itself.

Four minutes to midnight. The last minutes before the date changed passed across the phone screen. {name} divided the final page and wrote two headings: "Kept" and "Postponed." Whichever side he filled first, the other would remain empty tonight.

description_if_known.kept_clean_hands:
On the last night of the first year, {name} set the first notebook page beside the phone. Beneath "{notebook_motive}" and "3 billion won. Five years" came twelve months of rent, transit, money in, and losses.

The two million won from the first month was absent. After blocking the offer to lend out his account, {name} had set a 4:20 a.m. alarm. Money never taken left no figure, and the ledger alone did not show how he had spent the hours afterward.

Total assets: {assets}. The conversation list held the names of people he had met this year beside messages he had never answered. Four minutes to midnight, {name} divided the last page into "Kept" and "Postponed." Calling his hands clean did not fill either column for him.
description_if_known.escaped_dirty_money:
On the last night of the first year, {name} reread "{notebook_motive}" and "3 billion won. Five years." The two million won taken in the first month and the later receipt for a 1.5 million won return sat on separate lines.

After learning that victims' money had passed through his account, he blocked the numbers and closed it. Even after the 1.5 million won return was accepted, requests for further confirmation and the scope of his responsibility remained. No single figure said what was over and what was not.

Total assets: {assets}. Beside that number were promises kept and messages unanswered. Four minutes to midnight, {name} divided the last page into "Kept" and "Postponed." Filling either side first would not erase the figures on the other.
description_if_known.fell_to_darkness:
On the last night of the first year, {name} moved down the page beneath "{notebook_motive}" and "3 billion won. Five years." Two million won in the first month; three million after that. Only the amounts occupied the income column. The sources were blank.

The recruiter contacted him from a new number and sent the next account number. The three sets {name} had handed over already occupied amount fields; the new message remained at the top of the conversation list.

Total assets: {assets}. Unanswered names remained in the conversation list. Four minutes to midnight, {name} divided the last page into "Kept" and "Postponed." The pen would not descend under either heading.
description_if_known.jaehyuk_scammed:
December.

The year Jaehyuk disappeared. The year the account ran dry. The year of the real bottom.

The first line of the notebook still read, "{notebook_motive}" Most of the numbers beneath it had been erased.

Still here, though.

Looked at the ceiling of the room where he lived now. Its outline remained after the light went out.
description_if_known.entered_network:
December.

The year of meeting Im Sangchul's people. Learning a little of how that world works.

Under the notebook's first line, "{notebook_motive}," names he had never known a year ago had multiplied.

What that means going forward — still unknown.

Looked at the ceiling of the room where he lived now. Its outline remained after the light went out.
description_if_known.hit_rock_bottom:
December.

The year of seeing the real bottom. Now {name} knows exactly where it is.

Eraser dust clung to the notebook's first line, "{notebook_motive}" He had not erased the sentence.

Climbed back from it. Not all the way — but back.

Looked at the ceiling of the room where he lived now. Its outline remained after the light went out.

description_memory_if_known.m3_ledger_reasons_named: Following the brief reasons on the March page brought the days and hours behind twelve months of figures back into view.
description_memory_if_known.m3_ledger_totals_only: The March total was exact. Everything it could not count still had to be written separately.
description_memory_if_known.obligation_receipt:demo_collision:select: On Friday of Week 24, {name} called his father first. He still learned neither the diagnosis nor when he might go to Changwon, but he wrote down when to call again.

On Friday of Week 24, {name} sent the first month-end discrepancy sheet assigned to him at Hanbit Distribution at 5:59 p.m. He left unverified figures for a Monday site recheck instead of inventing them.

On Friday of Week 24, {name} submitted the City Facilities worksheet. In Week 28, a text with the same application number said there would be no interview. The submission and its result now stood on the same line.
On Friday of Week 24, {name} submitted the City Facilities worksheet and received an automated confirmation. The work itself was now part of his application record.
On Friday of Week 24, {name} reached the store in time for Daeun's night shift. Their check-in stopped whenever a customer entered, but {name} was the one who had gone to see her.
On Friday of Week 24, {name} messaged Jaehyuk first and asked about his week. Their conversation, with no talk of money, continued past six.
On Friday of Week 24, {name} left Sangchul's business card in the drawer and reconciled his own spending first. Rent, food, transit, and phone payments remained together on one ledger page.
On Friday of Week 24, {name} took an urgent overnight loading shift and earned 280,000 won. The day's pay and the strain in his palms and lower back entered the same ledger.
On Friday of Week 24, {name} set one alarm and put the phone face down. With every problem still unresolved, he chose sleep instead of pushing through one more night.
description_memory_if_known.obligation_receipt:demo_collision:deferr: That day, he neither called his father nor set a time for the next call.
The first month-end discrepancy sheet assigned to him at Hanbit Distribution passed its six o'clock deadline. One duty from that first assigned close remained as a blank in the notebook.
The City Facilities worksheet was not submitted. There was no automated receipt, and no result to wait for.
Though he knew when Daeun worked nights, {name} did not go to the store that day. The check-in he could have offered first was left for later.
{name} could have checked in with Jaehyuk first, but he did not start the conversation that day. Unsent words left no trace in the Kakao chat list.
The month's receipts stayed on the desk, and {name} did not reconcile his spending. Finding out where his own money had gone was postponed too.
{name} did not take the urgent overnight loading shift. Neither the 280,000 won nor the strain it would have left in his palms and lower back appeared in the ledger.
Lying down and tending to his body was pushed aside. The year's final page held not only the work he finished, but another night he endured.

choices.text: Finish the notebook — postpone sleep and record every gain beside what it cost
choices.result_text:
{name} spread the receipts by date and wrote the name postponed beside each amount. One line read "Gained," the next "Given up." Neither total resolved cleanly.

Past midnight, he erased neither the first promise nor the three billion won. By the time he glued down the last receipt, the celebration outside had stopped. One corner of the paper slowly lifted.

choices.text: Open Father's contact — leave tonight's accounting unsettled
choices.result_text:
{name} closed the notebook and opened Father's contact. Only the name, number, and surviving call times remained. There was no voice in them. He typed a New Year's greeting, then erased it without sending. No single record could cover the fact that no one would receive it.

A receipt slipped from the cover behind the desk after midnight. {name} did not turn on the light to find it. Only then did he close the contact screen.

choices.text: Turn off both notebook and phone — answer nothing and sleep tonight
choices.result_text:
{name} reopened neither the conversation list nor tomorrow's date before switching off the phone. The notebook closed with both "Kept" and "Postponed" empty.

A countdown came through the wall after the light went out. He kept his eyes closed from ten to one. Even after the year changed, his hand did not emerge from beneath the blanket.

title: The Last Night of 36
description:
On the last night of 36, {name} took the stairs to the roof. A clinic notice about his own body sat in his coat. At the top of the call list remained Father's name, a number that could no longer be dialed.

The promise to bring Father first when he reached Gangnam could not be deleted from the calendar or transferred to someone else. One year remained, while the number of people who could see the arrival had already fallen by one. Mother's last message and the clinic reminder appeared on the same screen.

At the railing, {name} drew the final twelve months. The squares for the target, the body, and the people still able to answer overlapped. Each gust lifted first the one square where he could not write Father's name.

description_if_known.arc_y4_year_close_protected_relationship:
On the last night of 36, {name} opened the notebook on the rooftop railing. Two weeks earlier, he had secured actual time for a person and canceled the overlapping money work. Beside that date remained Father's name, a number he could no longer call.

One relationship kept did not replace the blank left by the last contact. He did not restore the canceled work either. Time for a person still here and a name that would not return crossed into the final year on separate lines.

Tonight's question was not whom to protect. It was how to carry the price already paid without erasing it.
description_if_known.arc_y4_year_close_protected_body:
On the last night of 36, {name} opened the notebook on the rooftop railing. The follow-up time he had confirmed for his own body two weeks earlier was printed on the notice inside his coat. Father's name remained in the call log, a number he could no longer call.

Choosing to care for his own body did not bring Father's time back. Father's absence did not require him to abandon his own care either. The two records occupied separate lines in the same ledger.

Tonight's question was not body or family. It was how to carry the price already paid into the next chapter.
description_if_known.arc_y4_year_close_protected_family:
On the last night of 36, {name} opened the notebook on the rooftop railing. One line held the issuer, amount, deadline, and response limit of the family bill he had verified two weeks earlier. Above it remained Father's name, a number he could no longer call.

Answering the bill did not replace the last contact. Father's absence did not erase the bill's terms. A life that had ended and responsibilities that remained pointed to different times on the same screen.

Tonight's question was not whether to protect family again. It was how to carry verified facts into the next chapter.
description_if_known.arc_y4_midpoint_receipt_seen:
On the last night of 36, {name} opened the notebook on the rooftop railing. The three lines locked at midyear remained, but the damaged year-end record could not prove every outcome. Father's name, a number he could no longer call, was not a guess. It was settled evidence.

{name} did not bring Father back, and he invented no unknown outcome for a person, his body, or family. He carried only the verified absence and the unknown blanks into the next chapter on separate lines.

Each gust lifted Father's name and the unknown spaces with different weight.
description_if_known.year3_weighted:
On the last night of 36, {name} began counting the floors halfway up to the roof. The envelope holding last year's two documents remained inside the notebook. This year's clinic notice and the name of the last person contacted lay on top.

The ability to feel a burden as a burden remained. He had begun to tell what could be put down as weight alone from what would make him lighter by taking part of him too. In the final year's calendar, work for the target, time for his body, and a date promised to someone demanded the same square.

{name} spread the blank calendar over the railing. Without one hand holding it down, the paper lifted. The cold left the same mark in his palm as last year.
description_if_known.year3_eyes_open:
On the last night of 36, {name} took the stairs to the roof. The two documents kept together at the Han River last year still remained unlocked. This year a clinic notice about his body and the name of the last person contacted had joined them.

Refusing to pretend had slowed every choice. But carrying everything visible also required space. With one year left, work for money, an examination postponed, and a date promised to someone occupied the same square.

{name} drew twelve months on the railing. Seeing Gangnam's light and the darkness beneath it together was no longer enough. Actual time now had to be assigned to one or the other.
description_if_known.year3_avoidant:
On the last night of 36, {name} paused for breath on the stairs to the roof. Since locking the files and clearing every conversation alert at the Han River, the screen had stayed quiet and his pace had increased. This year's clinic notice and the name of the last person contacted now appeared over that lock screen.

He remembered the relief after deleting the words before he remembered whose they were. The final year's calendar stayed neat if it held only work for money. Adding the examination and other people's time made the squares overlap.

{name} spread the blank calendar on the railing. Empty squares alone could not show whether he had been running forward or running away.
description_if_known.sangchul_truth_known:
The last night of 36.

Knew the truth, made the choices, watched the results accumulate.

Four years of decisions are what {name} is now.

Whether that's right or wrong — the ending hasn't come yet.
description_if_known.crossed_line:
The last night of 36.

There was a year a line got crossed. Something shifted gradually after that.

What's done is done. Took a long time to accept that.

Accepted now. This is just who {name} is.

choices.text: Enter even the blanks from four years—do not pretend the price disappeared
choices.result_text:
{name} wrote what he had kept and what he had missed in letters of the same size. He did not restore a schedule already canceled or invent a completion time for something left undone.

On the final line, he wrote: The cost is part of my record. Even when the wind lifted the paper, the ink hid neither side.

choices.text: Write the limits of what the final year can bear in money and time
choices.result_text:
{name} listed how much more money he could lose, which time could no longer move, and how many nights he could still surrender. He left the boundary protected two weeks earlier in place and marked only the new promises he could not accept beyond it.

The plan grew smaller and matched the facts. Gray rooftop concrete showed through one small blank.

choices.text: Write no verdict; seal the ledger and reopen it on the next chapter's first day
choices.result_text:
Without erasing a record, {name} placed the notebook and notices in one envelope. He wrote neither that he had been right nor that he would do everything next time.

On the envelope, he wrote only the date of the next chapter's first day. The wind stopped when the rooftop door closed.
